subject: Clarification on Feb invoice token delta and EU VAT handling
messages:
From: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@patchwork.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts@patchwork.ai
Date: 2027-02-27T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Discrepancy on Feb invoice — 12k token delta and VAT applied

Hi Sean / Marissa,

We just received invoice #INV-20270228 and are seeing a ~12k token difference between our internal counters and the usage listed on the invoice. The invoice also shows VAT applied to the overage line for our EU entity — we thought the purchase was on our UK subsidiary (VAT-exempt for intra‑EU service per our PO).

Details:
- Invoice: INV-20270228 (attached)
- Redwood line: 62,420 tokens overage
- Our telemetry: 50,215 tokens (app-level instrumentation, sampled requests)
- Example request_id: req_2027-02-14_8f4a1b

Can you help reconcile the delta and confirm whether VAT should have been charged on the overage? We need this reconciled for our accounts payable before 3/5.

Attaching our quick snapshot export of requests for Feb 14–16.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Taylor
Finance Lead | Patchwork Analytics
[Attachment: invoice_20270228.pdf]

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@patchwork.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-27T10:04:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Feb invoice — 12k token delta and VAT applied

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Leaving Marissa on the thread for account context and looping in Karthik from Billing/Usage to get a technical reconciliation.

Preliminary next steps:
- Karthik will pull the per-request ledger and compare the tokenization used in invoicing vs. your app-sampled counters. A common source of delta is prefix caching + batching at the runtime layer that changes token attribution per request.
- We'll confirm VAT logic for your account (we have EU VAT handling tied to the billing entity on file). If VAT was applied in error we will issue a corrected invoice and credit.
- To avoid a payment hold impacting your account, we can provisionally issue a one-off credit for the disputed amount (pending audit).

Karthik — can you pull the ledger for Patchwork (Deal DEAL-4821) for the Feb 1–28 window and specifically flag any batch-aggregation or reused KV-cache segments that could increase per-invoice tokens vs sampled telemetry? Attach the CSV export and a short note about rounding behavior.

Emma — I’ll keep you posted; aiming to get an answer within 48 hours.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0136
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@patchwork.ai>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-28T14:37:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Feb invoice — 12k token delta and VAT applied

Hi Emma — thanks for flagging. I pulled the detailed ledger and attached the per-request export (usage_export_2027-02.csv). Summary of findings below.

Summary findings (Feb 1–28, Patchwork Analytics):
- Invoice tokens (Redwood billing): 62,420 tokens (matches what invoicing engine aggregated).
- Runtime-logged tokens (per-request ledger we use for billing): 62,412 tokens — difference of 8 tokens attributable to rounding at the per-batch end.
- Your sampled telemetry (50,215) appears to be application-level sampling (every Nth request) and does not include internal prefix cache replays and automated system prompts used by your workflows. Those pieces make up the ~12k gap when extrapolated from a sampled view.

Key technical notes:
- Batching and KV cache reuse: for requests that hit the prefix cache we charge for total generated tokens per RPC; if your sampled instrumentation aggregates only user prompts, that will undercount.
- Rounding: our per-batch accounting rounds token counts to the nearest integer after continuous batching aggregation; that explains the small 8-token discrepancy between our ledger and the invoicing table (already reconciled in the invoice).
- VAT: For DEAL-4821 we have billing entity recorded as Patchwork Analytics Ltd (UK), VAT id on file: GB999888777. However, the invoice in question used the EU VAT flow because the contract amendment from 2026-11 that switched billing entity to the EU holding org did not fully sync to the billing export. That led to VAT being included on the overage line.

Proposed remediation:
1) We will reissue a corrected invoice with VAT removed for the overage line once you confirm the correct billing entity (Patchwork Analytics Ltd vs Patchwork EU AG).
2) Because this was our sync error, Redwood will issue a provisional credit covering the VAT amount (estimated €1,420) immediately as a credit note (provisional_credit_note_4821.pdf attached). This will be applied to your account while we process the corrected invoice.
3) I attached usage_export_2027-02.csv (redacted request bodies) and a short reconciliation worksheet showing where the 12k difference comes from (sampling extrapolation + internal prompts).

Attachments: usage_export_2027-02.csv, provisional_credit_note_4821.pdf

Next steps from your side:
- Confirm which legal entity should be billed for Feb (Patchwork Analytics Ltd [UK VAT ID GB999888777] OR Patchwork EU AG [VAT: DE123456789]).
- If you confirm UK entity, we’ll push the corrected invoice and confirm the credit application within 72 hours.

If you want, we can also run a one-time audit export for the specific request_ids you supplied (req_2027-02-14_8f4a1b) to show token breakdown per step.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@patchwork.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, accounts@patchwork.ai
Date: 2027-03-01T15:43:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Feb invoice — 12k token delta and VAT applied

Hi Karthik / Sean — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear breakdown. Confirming: the correct billing entity is Patchwork Analytics Ltd (GB999888777). Please proceed with the corrected invoice and apply the provisional credit.

Also: two small asks so my AP team can clear payment today:
- Can you attach the short reconciliation worksheet (the per-batch delta summary) as a PDF?
- Please send the corrected invoice PDF and the credit note via DocuSign (we use that link to accept amended invoices in our Payables workflow). A DocuSign link in an email helps our automated ingestion.

If you can get those items to us today, we’ll process payment for the undisputed amount and mark the remaining line as pending until the corrected invoice arrives.

Appreciate the quick handling.

Best,
Emma
Emma Taylor
Finance Lead | Patchwork Analytics
[accounts@patchwork.ai]
